person.headline: Chairman | @Currencies Direct
person.about_me:
Antony Jenkins, CBE, is Founder, Chair and CEO of 10x Banking, the cloud-native core banking provider tackling legacy challenges for banks. Antony’s 40+ year career in the banking and financial technology sector has included leadership roles at some of the best-known names in the financial services sector, including serving as the CEO of Barclays and his current role as an external member of the Prudential Regulation Committee at the Bank of England. Antony’s board roles also include Group Chairman of Redpin, the leading UK non-bank provider of foreign exchange and international payment services. Additionally, he is passionate about the power of education and will become Chancellor of Manchester Metropolitan University in January 2025.

Antony was born in Blackburn, Lancashire and raised in the North West, where his father was production manager at a pottery factory. He studied Philosophy, Politics and Economics (PPE) at University College, Oxford before beginning his career in finance with Barclays in 1983. He subsequently moved to Citigroup, eventually heading up their branded credit card division before returning to Barclays, where he became CEO in 2012. He has also served on the boards of Visa Europe Ltd, Absa Group, Barclays Group, Fannie Mae, Blockchain.com and chaired Business in the Community and the Institute for Apprenticeships and Technical Education.

Antony founded London-based 10x Banking in 2016 - a company that provides banks around the world with a next-generation core platform to enable accelerated innovation and world-class customer experiences. In his role as Chair and CEO, he leads the company’s mission to enable a new era of financial inclusivity, prosperity and security by providing banks with the next-generation core banking platform they need to better serve their customers and improve the lives and livelihoods of billions of people across the world.
 
Antony was awarded a CBE for services to business in the Queen’s Birthday Honours in June 2021 and continues to be passionate about the imperative for banks to adopt and integrate best-in-breed technologies to better serve diverse customers.

person.headline: Director of Community Services | @Guild Care
person.about_me:
I’m so fortunate to have found where I’m meant to be! Reshaping both the local and national conversation around dementia with an incredible team of people.  Currently in West Sussex but soon to be across the Country!

A Dementia diagnosis is life altering for individuals and families – something I’ve personally experienced in my family with 3 grandparents with various types. I know how overwhelming and difficult to navigate that can be even with my background in Social Care & Public Health. 

Having worked in various and some senior roles in local government for 24 years and commissioning services to keep older people independent at home, I knew that there was still a gap when it came to dementia services.  Suddenly someone would get a diagnosis and the doors to activities and services were shut......I feel incredibly fortunate to now be in a position to change that and honour each of my grandparents memory.  

I completed my MBA and then up popped the role at the Charity. I made what was considered a "brave" decision and left Local Government after 24 years long service BUT I knew it was right.  I project managed the call centre into Sage House, recruited a fab team (39 at the time of writing!) and introduced enough policies and procedures to shake a stick at.....then we opened.  I knew even back then that I will never do something as completely satisfying and important again.  

Sage House literally helps change people’s lives… we have an incredible team of Wayfinders who support the whole family through their individual journey providing guidance, advice, emotional support and so much more.  We also host Activities daily that help stimulate and connect people (the smiles speak for themselves!), to our many Support Groups and Personal Care services (we have bathing, hair and therapy rooms too!), but not forgetting our Day Breaks providing respite for Carers with 1:3 care by another amazing team.

I’m just the CEO, but every single day I’m humbled by the impact of the services we provide. The importance of having a community hub/destination with a brilliant café at the heart of it, and the inspiring team that supports everyone that touches our service is evident daily.  

Next step is to make this a national offer through our blueprint.

Dementia Support: we're changing the narrative… so join us and start a hub in your community 😊. If I can do it anyone can! 

Learn more about what we do and visit: www.dementiasupport.org.uk/start-a-hub
